title: Progressive KV-tier quantization and batch-aware memory shaping
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: evaluate a progressive, tiered quantization strategy for the KV cache that reduces GPU memory usage while keeping downstream quality regressions within an acceptable SLO. The experiment mixes FP8/INT8/INT4 encodings across cache tiers and dynamically selects tiers based on request cohort, sequence-length, and batching regime. We need to measure trade-offs between memory savings, token latency under continuous batching, and model-generation quality across representative workloads.

Scope:
- Implement prototype pipeline to encode/serve KV cache in 3 fidelity tiers: high (FP32/FP16), mid (FP8/INT8), low (INT4 with residual compensation buffer).
- Route requests to tiers at runtime using a lightweight cohort selector that uses features: recent prefix similarity, request length, user tier, and current batch depth.
- Integrate with continuous-batching scheduler to observe latency and batching interactions; enforce latency SLOs with soft penalties in selection.
- Collect metrics: memory footprint (per-GPU and per-shard), per-token latency (p50/p95), generation quality (exact-match on eval sets, token-level KL, BLEU where applicable, and a human-annotated quality delta on 1k samples), and downstream error/timeout rates.

Experiment plan:
1) Offline encoding probe: convert existing KV dumps from runtime-1.18 to three candidate encodings and measure reconstruction error and simulated decode quality.
2) Microbenchmarks on a single-GPU staging cluster: evaluate throughput/latency of reading/writing compressed KVs under different batch sizes and concurrent requests.
3) Shadow runs on Canary fleet (5% traffic): enable route decision but keep results compared against baseline (no quant). Log divergences and fallback events.
4) Controlled A/B: run 10% traffic on quantized tiers for non-critical customers with canary rollback if defined quality thresholds breach.

Success criteria:
- Stable memory reduction >= 35% on average across typical conversation lengths without increasing 95th-percentile latency by more than 10% for targeted SLOs.
- Quality regressions: automatic metric thresholds must be under 0.8% delta for task-specific EM or equivalent; human-review flagged regressions must be <1.5% on sampled dialogs.
- No increase in production error rate or timeouts attributable to KV decompression.

Risks & mitigations:
- Decompression CPU/GPU overhead may increase latency: mitigate by prefetch+async decompression and hardware-friendly kernels.
- Bitpacking edge cases for short prefixes could hurt quality: implement prefix-preserve policy to keep earliest K tokens unquantized.
- Migration complexity across model versions: add model-compatibility metadata for each cached entry and fallback to full-fidelity on mismatch.

2025-02-22: Miguel implemented base INT4 packing routine; microbenchmarks show ~42% memory reduction on synthetic KV blobs, p50 latency increased by 3.2% under batch depth 8.
2025-02-24: Security review reminder: although cache entries contain embeddings, confirm KMS metadata for private deployments. Assigned to Security for signoff (ticket sent).
2025-02-26: PR 1543 opened for FP8 kernels and INT4 packer. Waiting on infra tests. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1543
2025-03-01: Offline distortion sweep completed. FP8 median reconstruction error < 0.6%, INT8 < 1.4%, INT4 w/ residual buffer < 3.8%. Added these numbers to the artifacts bucket and dashboard.

2025-03-03: Engineering review notes: need a fast-path for short prefix requests to avoid compaction artifacts. Decision: preserve first 32 KV tokens at FP16 in the low tier. Logged design update in Confluence.

2025-03-05: Canary gating checklist created. Blockers: extended infra stress tests failing on burst scenarios (memory oom on a mixed-tenant test). Root-cause points to edge-case in shard eviction; mitigation patch authored by infra (PR link included).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Prototype integrated with batch scheduler and KV store; 2) Offline distortion swept and documented; 3) Microbenchmarks show memory savings >=35% with p95 latency penalty <=10%; 4) Canary run plan + rollback criteria approved by SRE and Applied ML.
